does: Scores for the AI the stats functors of one spell: clamps the spell's ranges through its eoc::spell::ModificationContainerComponent, scores the functors with CalculateAiScoreStatsFunctors, and scores the success functors again weighted by the spell's success chance (its sixth argument, a float on the stack) after the archetype's stupidity modifier (esv::AiHelpers::GetAiHitChance: chance moved toward the modifier 0xBD), adding both into the result.

evidence.says: creates an AiScore, reads the ModificationContainerComponent of the spell's source, calls CalculateAiScoreStatsFunctors once or twice and merges with weight 1.0
A counter on every function over a play of the prologue shows it called only while a fight was on, from 16 places in the AI decision code, about 17 800 calls
the Toolkit's copy calls GetAiHitChance on its float argument and AiScoreInternal::ApplyChance with the result, logging 'Adjusting spell success chance ... for AI stupidity'

on a goblin's turn the sixth argument was 0.2, 0.5 and 0.45 for the goblin against the host - the values GK.Rolls.Chance gives at that moment for Target_SacredFlame, Target_MainHandAttack and Target_Bite_GiantSpider, the three spells of its candidates; 1.0 for spells with no roll
EoCServer.dll exports this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows

questions.ask: the name rests on the order of the Toolkit's names and on the spell modifications it reads; a probe of code:esv::AiHelpers::CalculateAiScoreSpellStatsFunctors with a goblin casting a known spell would tie the call to the spell id
which argument names the spell, so that each chance is tied to its spell by more than its value
